before.title: Brake Rotor Warping / Front Brake Vibration
before.description: Many FX35 owners report steering wheel shake or pedal pulsation during braking, usually traced to front rotor thickness variation and heat-related brake judder. The heavy curb weight and sporty driving style of the FX35 can accelerate front rotor wear, especially with lower-quality replacement pads and rotors.
before.solution: Diagnosis includes measuring rotor runout and thickness variation, checking caliper slide movement, and inspecting pad deposits. Repair generally involves replacing front rotors and pads together, cleaning and lubricating slide pins, and torquing wheels properly to prevent repeat distortion. Typical cost is about $250-$700 depending on parts quality and whether calipers or hoses also need service.
symptoms: Front-end vibration at highway speeds during braking

citations.title: NHTSA complaints citing brake vibration and rotor issues on Infiniti FX35

communityRecommendations.content: Owners frequently recommend coated premium rotors for better corrosion resistance and more consistent braking feel.
Quality ceramic pads are commonly recommended to reduce dust and improve daily-driver smoothness.
Torque lug nuts evenly with a torque wrench; uneven wheel torque is a common contributor to repeat brake pulsation complaints.

proposal.title: Brake Rotor Warping / Front Brake Vibration
proposal.description: Infiniti service bulletin ITB00-024I applies to all Infiniti vehicles and defines brake judder as vibration felt through the vehicle, steering wheel or brake pedal while braking. The bulletin identifies rotor thickness variation and/or rotor runout as the cause; brake-pedal pulsation and, in severe cases, steering-wheel oscillation can result.
proposal.solution: Verify the condition with the driver and a road test. Infiniti directs technicians to correct brake judder by machining the rotors with an approved on-car brake lathe. If a rotor is replaced, index it to the axle hub for minimum runout, tighten lug nuts evenly with a torque wrench, and burnish serviced brakes as specified in ITB00-024I.

before.title: Camshaft / Crankshaft Position Sensor Failure
before.description: The FX35 commonly develops intermittent failures of the camshaft position sensors and sometimes the crankshaft position sensor, causing stalling, hard starts, or limp operation. Heat and age degrade the sensor electronics, and this issue is widely reported across Nissan/Infiniti VQ applications of the era.
before.solution: Diagnosis is done by scanning for correlation or sensor circuit codes and monitoring live RPM/cam signals during crank and road test. Repair usually involves replacing one or both cam sensors and sometimes the crank sensor, preferably with OE-quality parts because low-cost sensors often cause repeat faults. Typical repair cost is about $150-$450 depending on how many sensors are replaced and labor rates.

citations.title: NHTSA complaints mentioning stalling and cam/crank sensor faults on Infiniti FX35

communityRecommendations.content: Owners strongly prefer OE supplier sensors because many aftermarket no-name sensors trigger repeat codes or intermittent no-starts.
Replace both bank cam sensors together if mileage is high, since the second sensor often fails soon after the first.
For crank sensor replacement, owners often choose a known OE-quality brand to avoid false RPM signal dropouts.

before.title: Front Suspension Clunk / Worn Control Arm Bushings
before.description: The FX35 is well known for front-end clunks, loose steering feel, and uneven tire wear caused by worn front lower control arm bushings, compression rod bushings, and sway bar end links. The vehicle's weight and sporty suspension tuning accelerate bushing wear, especially on rough roads and higher-mileage examples.
before.solution: Diagnosis involves checking for play in the lower control arms, tension/compression rods, ball joints, and sway bar links while the suspension is loaded. Repair usually means replacing the worn arm assemblies or bushings and then performing a four-wheel alignment. Typical cost is about $300-$1,000 depending on whether one side or multiple front suspension components are renewed.
symptoms: Vibration during braking or road impacts

citations.title: NHTSA complaints for Infiniti FX35 front suspension noise and control arm wear

communityRecommendations.content: Owners often use complete arm assemblies to save labor and restore ride quality instead of pressing in bushings only.
Have the suspension inspected with the vehicle at normal ride height; some worn bushings are missed when the control arms hang free.
Sway bar links are a common companion repair when chasing front-end clunks.

before.title: Fuel Gauge Sending Unit Failure
before.description: A common Nissan/Infiniti issue on this era of FX35 is inaccurate fuel level readings caused by wear or contamination of the fuel level sending unit inside the tank. Owners report the gauge sticking, dropping suddenly, or showing empty with fuel still in the tank, sometimes accompanied by a check engine light.
before.solution: Diagnosis involves comparing scan-tool fuel level data with actual tank fill amount and checking for sender-related codes. Repair typically requires replacing the affected fuel level sender or pump module assembly through the access panel under the rear seat/cargo area, depending on configuration. Typical cost is about $300-$800 using quality parts and new tank seal hardware.
symptoms: Fuel gauge reads empty when tank is not empty
Low fuel warning comes on too early
Check engine light with EVAP/fuel level correlation faults

citations.title: NHTSA complaints for Infiniti FX35 inaccurate fuel gauge readings

communityRecommendations.content: Owners usually recommend OE-quality fuel level components because cheap modules can cause continued gauge inaccuracies.
If the gauge is erratic, track mileage manually until the sender is repaired to avoid running the tank dry.
Replace the tank seal and inspect the electrical connector for heat damage whenever the module is removed.

before.title: Radiator Crack and Coolant / Transmission Cross-Contamination
before.description: On first-generation FX35 models with the automatic transmission cooler integrated into the radiator, internal radiator failure can allow coolant and ATF to mix. Owners report radiator tank cracking or internal cooler failure, which can quickly damage the transmission if not caught early.
before.solution: Diagnosis includes checking the radiator and overflow bottle for oily residue, inspecting ATF for a milky appearance, and pressure-testing the cooling system. Repair typically requires replacing the radiator and thoroughly flushing the cooling and transmission systems; if contamination was severe, transmission repair or replacement may also be needed. Costs range from about $400 for early radiator replacement to $5,000+ if the transmission has been damaged.

citations.title: NHTSA complaints involving radiator failure and transmission damage on FX35

communityRecommendations.content: If the original radiator is still installed on a high-mileage first-gen FX35, many owners replace it preventively rather than risk transmission contamination.
Owners often recommend a quality replacement radiator instead of the cheapest unit because fitment and cooler reliability matter here.
Check ATF color regularly after any overheating event; catching contamination early can save the transmission.

before.title: Timing Chain Guide / Whine from Front Cover
before.description: Early VQ35DE-equipped FX35 models are known for a whining or supercharger-like noise caused by wear in the timing chain guides and related front timing components. Infiniti issued service information for replacing the primary timing chain, guides, tensioners, and sprockets when abnormal noise is present, most commonly on earlier production years.
before.solution: Diagnosis usually starts by confirming a front-engine whine that changes with RPM and ruling out accessory bearings by removing the drive belts briefly. Repair typically involves removing the front timing cover and replacing the timing chain, guides, tensioners, and often cam/crank sprockets using updated parts; labor is substantial because of front cover access. Independent shop repair commonly runs about $1,500-$3,000 depending on how many timing components are replaced.
symptoms: Whining noise from front of engine
Persistent front cover noise after belt inspection

communityRecommendations.content: Confirm the noise is not from an idler pulley, alternator, or A/C compressor before authorizing timing cover work.
Owners generally recommend using OEM-style timing components because cheap kits have mixed durability on the VQ35DE.
If the front cover is already off, many owners replace water pump seals and inspect cam/crank seals at the same time to avoid duplicate labor.
